PullRequest.Title: sessions: Left-align Remotes inline actions
PullRequest.Body:

Stacked on #343821. Refs #343790.

Left-align Remotes inline actions within their column instead of right-aligning them. Hover and keyboard-focus visibility are unchanged. Updates the existing alignment regression test.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed with zero compilation errors.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser webkit --browser chromium-msedge --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesWidget.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 36 tests per browser.
- `node build\hygiene.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\browser\media\remotesWidget.css src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesWidget.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Manual check: open Remotes, hover or keyboard-focus a remote or section row, and confirm the actions align to the left of their column.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous click path, per-row invocation, allocating service getter, and one-provider-per-configured-entry reconciliation are directly established in the repository. Exact delay depends on users' remote-catalog size, but the quadratic CPU/allocation mechanism is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU comparisons plus arrays and normalized entry/connection object allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(N^2) work and allocations for N displayed configured remote environments (N getter snapshots of N configured entries), rather than one O(N) index build.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased picker-open latency and CPU/GC pressure on the UI thread
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With global Manage enabled, the previous ternary assigned `undefined` directly for every row and did not read or scan the configured remote catalog while constructing picker items.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Opening the Environment picker with global Manage enabled now snapshots, normalizes, and linearly scans all configured remote entries separately for each displayed remote environment.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 231 adds `this.isManagedInRemotes(environment)` inside `this.environments.get().map(...)`, so it executes once per displayed environment. The added helper's line 289 reads `remoteAgentHostService.configuredEntries` on every call; that getter maps the entire configured-entry collection and `_normalizeEntry` copies normalized entries/connections before `.find` scans it.
Findings.Title: Index configured remotes once before mapping picker rows
Findings.Impact: For users with a large configured remote fleet, clicking the Environment control can synchronously allocate and scan quadratically before the popup appears, causing input latency and avoidable GC pauses.
Findings.Evidence: `showPicker()` synchronously maps all environments before calling `actionWidgetService.show`. `isManagedInRemotes` reads `configuredEntries` per remote; `RemoteAgentHostService.configuredEntries` is implemented as `_configuredEntries.get().map(entry => this._normalizeEntry(entry))`, and normalized-address entries are copied with new entry and connection objects. Entry-driven contributions register one session provider for each configured SSH/WSL/etc. entry, so with N configured remotes the picker generally has N remote environments and performs N full N-entry snapshots plus N linear finds.
Findings.Recommendation: When `showManage` is true, read `configuredEntries` once before mapping, build a map from address to connection, and have the per-environment check use that map; this preserves the entry-type rules while reducing picker-open work to O(N).

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Environment picker with global Manage enabled and a configured remote fleet
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click or keyboard activation calls `showPicker`, synchronously reads settings, maps every environment, classifies management ownership, builds menu actions, and only then calls `actionWidgetService.show`; the new configured-entry scans are therefore directly on popup-open latency.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the number N of visible remote session providers backed by configured entries; each of those rows scans the configured catalog of approximately N entries, yielding O(N^2) work without grouping or deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All classification, normalization, allocation, and scans run serially on the UI thread. There is no limiter or asynchronous overlap; N remote rows cause N sequential full catalog snapshots/scans.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The underlying `_configuredEntries` derived value is cached, but each `configuredEntries` property read remaps and normalizes the full collection into a fresh array; repeated warm picker opens and each row within one open receive no snapshot/index reuse. Provider lookup itself is a warm in-memory Map lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed ternary invokes the helper from the per-environment map, the helper reads the collection getter, and the getter implementation allocates/maps the full catalog on every read. Entry-driven provider reconciliation establishes approximately one displayed provider per configured entry.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on fleet size and hardware; small catalogs mask the cost, while users retaining tens to hundreds of SSH, WSL, tunnel, sandbox, or other hosts amplify it. The quadratic mechanism and UI-thread placement are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity regression: the diff replaces the previous constant per-row decision with repeated full-catalog snapshots and scans on the synchronous input path. Snapshotting/indexing once per open preserves behavior and makes it O(N).

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct a new chat widget and its environment/workspace controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New chat widget construction creates the environment picker and then always creates `WorkspacePicker` or `WebWorkspacePicker`; remote-host initialization was already required by the latter. The diff only resolves the same singleton slightly earlier in that constructor sequence.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One environment picker and one workspace picker per new-chat widget; singleton resolution remains once per service lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Construction is serial service injection with singleton reuse; no new concurrent task, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The remote-host service is a delayed singleton, but both desktop and web workspace pickers created immediately after the environment picker already inject it, so the added environment-picker injection does not add a new long-lived service initialization to this widget lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High, based on the unconditional picker construction and both constructors' injected `IRemoteAgentHostService`.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty: both platform picker variants visibly require the same singleton on the same widget construction path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No eager-work regression: the apparently new service dependency was already transitively instantiated by the immediately following workspace picker.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, hover, and keyboard-focus rows in the Remotes widget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On Remotes widget render, hover, focus, or layout, the browser resolves `justify-content` as `flex-start` instead of `flex-end`; no new DOM reads, writes, listeners, or relayout loops are added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing number of rendered remote rows; the diff adds no per-row nodes or additional style rules, so asymptotic render/layout work is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal browser style/layout scheduling is unchanged; there is no application-level queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retained-state behavior changes. Browser style calculation uses the same existing flex container and toolbar nodes; only the alignment value changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the single declaration change and unchanged hover/focus selectors and test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; this is a constant-time CSS value substitution on already-laid-out rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: left alignment changes geometry only and does not introduce extra rendering or layout work.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: When accessibility help content is requested, the existing configuration checks and telemetry trigger run, then one slightly longer string is pushed. No changed blocking operation or collection traversal is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per accessibility-help invocation; independent of providers, remotes, history, and session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous content-generation invocation; no fan-out or new asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Accessibility content is generated on demand with no changed cache lifecycle; the diff only extends one localized string.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the localized-string-only production change and assertion-only test update.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added text is a bounded constant-size allocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the bounded string-length increase is negligible and does not alter any expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and their relevant callers/services. Reported one synchronous quadratic picker-open regression; rejected eager service initialization, CSS layout, accessibility text, and test-only changes as non-regressions.
